evals.name: diagram-page
evals.prompt: No termino de entender cómo fluye una petición HTTP en nuestra plataforma: hay una CDN delante, luego un API gateway que aplica rate limiting, después el servicio, y una caché Redis que se consulta antes de tocar la base de datos. ¿Me lo puedes explicar visualmente?
evals.expected_output: A themed, self-contained HTML page with a diagram of the request path (labeled arrows, cache hit vs. miss), delivered through scripts/render.mjs and validated with scripts/check_artifact.mjs.
assertions: An HTML page file was written to the output directory.
The transcript shows the visual-explainer skill was loaded (SKILL.md read or the skill invoked).
The transcript shows check_artifact.mjs reporting that the page passes the page delivery check.
The diagram traverses the request path CDN → API gateway → service → Redis cache → database, and the cache hit vs. miss distinction is visible.
Arrows carry labels describing what happens (for example 'rate limit', 'cache miss'), not bare lines.
The figure has a caption that states a claim about the system, not a title that merely names it.
The page is themed through CSS custom properties (coherent palette and typography), not browser-default HTML.

evals.name: slidev-deck
evals.prompt: Monta en este proyecto un deck de Slidev de unas seis diapositivas que explique los tres estados de un fichero en Git (working directory, staging area y repositorio) a desarrolladores junior. Déjalo listo para previsualizar con `npm run slides:dev`.
evals.expected_output: A Slidev deck as project source (slides.md plus project wiring, no copied theme styles or local global layers), written after sharing a storyboard, with presenter notes, and validated with check_artifact.mjs --kind slidev.
assertions: A slides.md file was created in the project.
Before writing slides.md, the assistant shared a storyboard: an inventory of the source topics plus a per-slide mapping to a slide type and composition.
The transcript shows check_artifact.mjs reporting that the deck passes the slidev delivery check.
slides.md contains between 4 and 9 slides, each with a presenter note, and the first note states an estimated duration.
Each of the three Git file states gets real coverage, and at least one slide shows the transitions between them as a figure or visual composition rather than a bullet list.
Slide layouts vary; not every slide is the default layout with bullets.
slides.md contains no hardcoded colors; styling is left to the Slidev theme.
The deck is project source: no theme styles copied into the deck and no local global layers.

evals.name: deck-html
evals.prompt: Prepárame una presentación breve para enviar por email a otro equipo — un único fichero HTML autocontenido, nadie la va a mantener después. Tema: por qué importan los índices compuestos en PostgreSQL — el orden de las columnas, la regla del prefijo, y cuándo un índice no ayuda. Unas seis u ocho diapositivas.
evals.expected_output: A self-contained HTML deck (one-shot lifecycle picks the deck-html target over Slidev), built from a shared storyboard and passing check_artifact.mjs --kind deck-html.
assertions: An HTML deck file was written to the output directory.
A storyboard was shared before the deck was written.
The transcript shows check_artifact.mjs reporting that the deck passes the deck-html delivery check.
The Slidev CLI (@slidev/cli) was never invoked: the one-shot lifecycle picked the HTML target.
The result is a slide deck with viewport-sized slides and navigation, not a scrollable article.
It has 6 to 8 slides covering composite index column order, the prefix rule, and when an index does not help — each with real content, none dropped to fit.
Compositions vary across slides, and at least one slide uses a figure, table, or code sample instead of bullets.
Styling is coherent and token-based (CSS custom properties), with visible navigation chrome (progress, dots, counter or equivalent).

evals.name: table-trigger
evals.prompt: Compárame SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL y DuckDB en cuatro dimensiones: licencia, modelo de concurrencia, sistema de tipos y caso de uso ideal.
evals.expected_output: The 4×4 comparison renders as a semantic HTML table page; the chat reply is a short summary pointing to it, not a terminal table.
assertions: An HTML page file was written to the output directory, even though the user never asked for a page or a diagram.
The page contains a semantic HTML <table> element.
The final chat reply is a short prose summary that points the reader to the page for the full comparison.
The final chat reply does not reproduce the comparison inline as a markdown or ASCII table.

evals.name: fact-check
evals.prompt: Haz un fact-check del documento out/report.html contra el código real de este repositorio y corrígelo donde no diga la verdad.
evals.expected_output: out/report.html corrected in place (verifyToken, 60 minutes), original structure preserved, plus a verification summary classifying each checked claim.
assertions: The report names the function verifyToken, matching src/auth.js.
The expiry claim now says 60 minutes, matching EXPIRY_MINUTES in src/auth.js.
The true claim about the reason field distinguishing malformed from expired tokens was left standing.
The document's original structure and styling are preserved: it was corrected in place, not rewritten.
A verification summary was added stating what was checked and what changed, with a verdict per claim (for example verified / corrected).

evals.name: no-activation
evals.expected_output: The assistant answers with the corrected function directly; the visual-explainer skill is never invoked.
assertions: The reply returns the parseConfig function with error handling added.
The visual-explainer skill was never invoked: no skill call and no read of its SKILL.md.
No HTML page, diagram, or deck was produced.
